earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog refs for Bonkeng are wordlists/comparative Bantu only; no grammar, sketch, or phonology listed

sources.citation: SIL Electronic Survey Reports, country index 'Cameroon' (sil.org/silesr/indexes/countries.asp, Internet Archive copy 2012) and SIL Cameroon site search (silcam.org) for 'Bonkeng'.
sources.note: No survey report on Bonkeng exists in the ESR series (nearest: Lamberty 2002 on Abo and Barombi; Bakossi survey); SIL Cameroon search returns no results for Bonkeng.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalogue (search.language-archives.org), subject-language bvg and free-text 'Bonkeng'.
sources.note: Only one record for bvg: the Glottolog resource page. No archive deposits, wordlists or descriptions.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank (eds.) 2026. Glottolog 5.3, languoid page 'Bonkeng' (bonk1243) and its reference table (6 refs: Johnston 1919-22; Jacquot & Richardson 1956; Guthrie 1953; Valdau 1888, 1889; Dugast 1949 - all overview/comparative/wordlist).
sources.note: Nothing; no grammar, sketch or phonology is listed for Bonkeng. Title search of the whole Glottolog bibliography for 'Bonkeng'/'Bongkeng' returns 0 works.

sources.citation: Simons, Gary F. & Charles D. Fennig (eds.) 2017. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 20th ed., entry 'Bonkeng [bvg]' (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Nothing: gives names (Bongken, Bonkeng-Pendia, Bonkenge), 3,000 speakers (2000), Loum subdivision, A.14 Lundu-Balong, 'Unwritten'; no dialect/typology lines.

sources.citation: Maho, Jouni Filip. 2009. NUGL Online: The online version of the New Updated Guthrie List.
sources.note: Nothing; lists 'A14 Bonkeng bvg' (with A141 Bafo) as an inventory entry only.

sources.citation: Hedinger, Robert. 1984. The Manenguba languages (Bantu A.15, Mbo cluster) of Cameroon. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London (published 1987, SOAS).
sources.note: Nothing on Bonkeng prosody; Bonkeng (BNK, 'Bantu A.14', names Bonken/Bonkenge/Bongkeng-Pendia) appears only in the language-name inventory and in the lexicostatistic classification discussion ('BNK (Bonkeng) probably not [in the Mbo group] either'). The phonology chapters describe Akoose/Mbo-cluster varieties, not Bonkeng.

sources.citation: [Anonymous / administration du Cameroun]. 1934. Inventaire ethnique et linguistique du Cameroun sous mandat français. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 4(2): 203-208.
sources.note: Nothing: an ethnic/linguistic inventory with head-counts and notes on Duala/Bassa influence ('Les Bakoko ainsi que les tribus de race et de parler Bassa sont.. dans la zone d'influence du Douala'); no linguistic data.

sources.citation: Johnston, Harry H. 1919. A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages. Vol. I. Oxford: Clarendon Press (language no. 211 'Bonken' [= Bonkeng]: illustrative vocabulary pp. 630-640 with no. 212 Abo, 'Prefixes in Bonken and Abo' and location note pp. 640-641, source note in the bibliography: Johnston's own collection in the Cameroons 1886-88 plus Beba Bell); Vol. II. 1922. Oxford: Clarendon Press (Group OO chapter, one classificatory sentence on Bonken 211, p. ~162).
sources.note: Nothing. The Bonken material is an untoned comparative vocabulary (c. 250 glosses), a list of noun-class prefixes ('Class 1. M-, Mo-.. 8a. Fi- (Abo), I- (Bonken)..'), a location note and a source note; vol. II adds only 'BONKEN (211) and ABO (212).. are outlying members of Group OO (Sub-group OO b), which have been much in contact with and much affected by the Semi-Bantu languages of the north-east.' No tone marks, no remark on tone, accent or stress. Wordlist-plus-prefixes data only.

sources.citation: Binam Bikoi, Charles (ed.). 2012. Atlas linguistique du Cameroun (ALCAM), 2 vols. Yaounde: CERDOTOLA (entry Bonkeng [A14], Littoral).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: National atlas notice for Bonkeng; may cite unpublished local descriptions or wordlists, though ALCAM notices normally give no prosodic information.

sources.citation: Hedinger, Robert. 1987. The Manenguba Languages (Bantu A.15, Mbo Cluster) of Cameroon. London: SOAS. (published version of the 1984 thesis; appendix wordlists include BNK = Bonkeng items used for lexicostatistics).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only specialist work known to contain first-hand Bonkeng data (tone-marked wordlist items); would at most show tone marking, not a stress rule. The 1984 thesis held by the project already shows no prosodic statement for Bonkeng.

sources.citation: Guthrie, Malcolm. 1953. The Bantu Languages of Western Equatorial Africa. London: Oxford University Press for the International African Institute, pp. 15-21 (Lundu-Balong group A.10, incl. A.14 Bonkeng).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: no other copy located; the linked copy is a different work
sources.note: Glottolog's top-ranked reference; Guthrie sometimes adds one-line phonological remarks per group (e.g. tone), which would be the only printed typological note covering Bonkeng.

sources.citation: Any University of Yaounde I / Douala / Buea maitrise or DEA memoire of the type 'Esquisse phonologique du bonkeng' (existence unverified; not in SUDOC, HAL, theses.fr, Glottolog or OLAC).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Cameroonian departmental memoires are the usual only description for A.10 micro-languages; if one exists it would contain the tone/accent section.
